timecoded_text_to_speech.text: The universe is a vast expanse of space filled with numerous galaxies, each with its own unique set of characteristics and properties.
Astronomers have long been fascinated by the study of galaxies, and over the years, new technologies have been developed to help us learn more about these celestial objects.
One such technology is the James Webb Space Telescope, or Webb for short, which was recently launched by NASA in December 2021.
The Webb Telescope is a revolutionary new tool for astronomers, designed to help us see further into the universe than ever before.
Unlike its predecessor, the Hubble Space Telescope, which primarily observes visible and ultraviolet light, the Webb Telescope will focus on infrared light.
This is an important difference because many objects in the universe emit most of their light in the infrared part of the spectrum.
This means that the Webb Telescope will be able to observe objects that are invisible to other telescopes.
One of the key objectives of the Webb Telescope is to study the formation and evolution of galaxies.
